facts.text: Fairfield was founded in 1856 by clipper ship captain Robert H. Waterman, who named the town after his hometown in Connecticut.
In 1903 Fairfield became an incorporated city, having served as Solano County’s seat since 1858 after winning the race against Benicia.
The city hosts Travis Air Force Base, one of the largest military installations in the Bay Area, alongside the headquarters of Jelly Belly.
Fairfield’s Jelly Belly factory at 1 Jelly Belly Lane produces the iconic candy beans and displays a permanent bean art collection for visitors.
Located north of Suisun Bay, Fairfield sits within the California Coastal Ranges and borders the world’s largest saltwater marsh, Suisun Marsh.
The city’s historic landmarks include a working candy factory, a major Air Force base, restored courthouses, and volcanic parks.
